travel-seoul-01: Gyeongbokgung: focus on Geunjeongjeon main hall, two-tier dark tiled hip roof, red wooden columns and dancheong eaves on a raised pale stone terrace in a broad stone courtyard. Do not substitute a Chinese pagoda or mix multiple palace gates.
travel-seoul-02: Bukchon: narrow sloping residential lane, low hanok with curved gray tiled roofs, timber, pale plaster and stone walls. No Japanese torii or temple pagoda.
travel-seoul-03: N Seoul Tower: slim white concrete communications tower, broad enclosed observation pod near the top and slender antenna mast, standing above wooded Namsan hill.
travel-seoul-04: Cheonggyecheon: narrow restored urban stream below street level, pedestrian paths along both banks, stone edges, modest bridges and modern Seoul buildings above. Not a broad river.
travel-seoul-08: DDP: low flowing silver metal-clad building, rounded asymmetric organic curves and perforated/panelled surface; not a conventional skyscraper.
travel-seoul-09: Changdeokgung rear garden: traditional Korean tiled pavilion beside a quiet pond and mature woodland. Preserve restrained Joseon garden character.
travel-incheon-12: Songdo Central Park: planned waterside urban park with a broad artificial waterway and modern high-rise buildings, landscaped pedestrian banks.
travel-incheon-16: Incheon Dohobu government-office compound: modest Joseon timber halls with dark tiled roofs and red columns, open courtyard, not a monumental palace.
travel-busan-17: Haeundae: broad sandy beach, gently curving urban bay and dense modern coastal high-rises behind. No fantasy tropical island.
travel-busan-18: Gamcheon: densely packed pastel-colored low houses stepping down a steep hillside, narrow lanes, coastal city context. No Mediterranean domes.
travel-busan-19: Jagalchi: market interior with practical stainless counters, fresh seafood and water tanks, recognizable working Korean seafood market. No exotic invented fish.
travel-busan-20: Gwangan Bridge: long double-deck suspension bridge spanning the sea with two main towers and curved suspension cables. View from Gwangalli beach; do not depict a cable-stayed fan bridge.
travel-busan-21: Haedong Yonggungsa: Korean Buddhist tiled-roof temple buildings on rocky shoreline immediately beside blue sea, stone stairs and terraces. No inland mountain-only setting.
travel-busan-22: Beomeosa: Korean Buddhist temple halls and stone steps in wooded mountain setting, dark tiled roofs with colorful dancheong. No shoreline.
travel-suwon-25: Hwaseong: long stone-and-brick defensive wall with crenellations following gentle green terrain, Korean tiled-roof gate pavilion. Not the Great Wall of China.
travel-suwon-26: Hwahongmun: exactly seven stone water arches across a narrow stream, a single long traditional tiled-roof wooden pavilion above. Frontal view where all seven arches are visible.
travel-suwon-27: Korean Folk Village is in Yongin near Suwon, not central Suwon. Show reconstructed Joseon village houses with thatched and tiled roofs, earthen paths and low stone walls.
travel-jeju-30: Hallasan: summit crater Baengnokdam, broad volcanic crater basin within green/brown mountain slopes, partial shallow water is plausible. Not an erupting volcano or sharp Alpine spire.
travel-jeju-31: Seongsan Ilchulbong: coastal tuff cone with steep cliff sides, crown-like crater rim and broad grassy bowl, surrounded by blue sea on its seaward sides. No lava eruption.
travel-jeju-32: Manjanggul: dark basalt lava-tube passage with layered flow marks and irregular cooled lava surfaces, subdued neutral illumination. No fantasy glowing magma, ice or dominant limestone stalactite forest.
travel-jeju-33: Hyeopjae: pale sandy beach, clear shallow turquoise water, black volcanic rocks and low Biyangdo island offshore. No tropical palm forest.
travel-jeju-34: O'Sulloc tea fields: orderly low clipped green tea rows on gently rolling land on Jeju with volcanic island landscape. No hillside rice terraces.
travel-jeju-35: Jeju oreum: small grass-covered volcanic cone with smooth rounded flanks and crater depression, walking path for scale. Not a large active volcano.
travel-jeju-36: Haenyeo: adult and older women divers in black wetsuits, masks and fins, orange surface floats with mesh catch nets, near black basalt shore. Breath-hold diving: absolutely no scuba tanks or compressed-air regulators.
travel-jeju-37: Sanbangsan: massive rounded steep-sided volcanic dome rising prominently behind low coastal landscape, rugged rock face and greenery. No pointed Alpine peak.
travel-gyeongju-38: Bulguksa: Korean Buddhist temple stone terraces and stairs, wooden halls with dark tiled roofs, Silla stonework. Do not invent a many-storey wooden pagoda.
travel-gyeongju-39: Seokguram: seated stone Buddha in a circular granite grotto, serene face, lotus pedestal, right hand reaching toward the ground, draped robes. Educational illustration, not a claimed photograph taken inside.
travel-gyeongju-40: Daereungwon: several large smooth rounded grass-covered royal burial mounds among trees. No Egyptian pyramids or visible stone tomb entrances.
travel-gyeongju-41: Cheomseongdae: small gray granite observatory, square base, curved tapering cylindrical body with square opening midway, square crossbeam top. No roof, telescope or lighthouse lantern.
travel-gyeongju-42: Donggung and Wolji (formerly Anapji): reconstructed Korean tiled-roof pavilions beside landscaped pond, warm evening lights reflected in water, restrained accurate architecture.
travel-gyeongju-43: Hwangnidan-gil: low-rise hanok-style cafe/shop street, dark gray tiled roofs, timber fronts and walkable lane. Generic blank shop signs, no invented readable names.
